\paragraph{Vision token efficiency.}
Token pruning in ViTs is well studied: methods select tokens by learned binary masks~\cite{rao2021dynamicvit}, attention-guided reorganization~\cite{liang2022evit}, bipartite matching~\cite{bolya2023tome}, or window-level activation sparsity~\cite{chen2023sparsevit}, consistently removing 30--60\% of tokens with $<$1\% accuracy loss on classification. Adaptive approaches vary computation per input: TokenLearner~\cite{ryoo2021tokenlearner} learns spatial attention maps for compact token selection, A-ViT~\cite{yin2022avit} applies per-token halting that terminates patches at different network depths, and AdaViT~\cite{meng2022adavit} jointly adapts patch, head, and block usage. For VLMs, pruning extends to the language backbone: FastV~\cite{chen2024fastv} removes tokens after early LLM layers, LLaVA-PruMerge~\cite{shang2024prumerge} and FasterVLM~\cite{zhang2024fastervlm} use CLS-token attention from the visual encoder as an importance signal, FitPrune~\cite{ye2025fitprune} minimizes attention-distribution divergence to produce layerwise pruning recipes without training, and CrossGET~\cite{shi2024crossget} applies cross-modal guided token merging. We studied vision token pruning across seven VLA models (450M--7B) spanning three connector families on closed-loop robotic manipulation. Four findings emerge. (1)~The vision connector is strongly associated with pruning behavior along a four-class compressibility spectrum: uniformly critical, threshold-graded, smooth graded, and catastrophic cliff.
